root_cause: _score_charge_target's ch_damage paid the charger's whole expected melee damage even when it was several times the target's wounds left: at s7480 r3 P2 an Allarus remnant with 2 wounds left got ch_damage 15 (7.5 dmg x 2), the same as the 6-wound Allarus #2, and with the 97% chance and the 3" short-charge multipliers (x1.56) it scored 41.1 vs the full-health Blade Champion's 32.9. The kill itself is already paid by ch_can_wipe/ch_can_halve, so the excess was pure overkill. Second leg (found while checking the fix): even with the damage capped (remnant single 21.6 < BC 32.9) the T7-50 multi-target pass declared 'remnant + Blade Champion' (EV 36.0), because the remnant is the cheap low-roll leg; in play the charge move could not engage both and dropped the Blade Champion, so that declaration played out identically to the base (forced 'remnant + BC' vs base: E 0.00 [0,0] over 12 paired seeds, every game identical). The extra findings (s7465 r2 P1 Stormboyz, s7461 r3 P2 Battlewagon) have a different cause (low-odds / low-damage multi-target declarations with no gross overkill) and are not addressed by this narrow design.
fix_summary: FIX_CHARGE_TARGET (1.0) with CHARGE_TARGET_OVERKILL_RATIO 2.0. Two gated conditions on existing rules, no new scoring: (CT-OVERKILL) in _score_charge_target, when expected melee damage >= 2 x the target's remaining wounds, ch_damage uses the remaining wounds instead of the expected damage (near-exact kills like 7.1 vs 7 or 8.9 vs 7 untouched); (CT-COMBO) in _evaluate_best_charge, a target in that gross-overkill state is left out of the multi-target (T7-50) combos - it still competes as a single target, and a low roll still re-picks it post-roll via _select_post_roll_charge_targets. Logs [CHARGE_TARGET] at each capped evaluation and each combo exclusion. FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0 restores the base exactly (test checks both the term and the decision).

fires: [CHARGE_TARGET] lines (each capped target evaluation incl. post-roll re-scoring, plus each combo exclusion) in the fix replays from the saved position to the end of the next battle round, both players: s7480 r3 P2 3 (1 combo exclusion; changed the finding decision), s7480 r3 P1 7 (1), s7470 r2 P2 18 (3), s7465 r2 P2 7 (1), s7465 r2 P1 33 (12), s7461 r3 P2 25 (12), s7466 r3 P2 0. At the 7 decision positions it changed exactly 1 decision (the finding). Orks charge pools (Stormboyz/Battlewagons vs Gretchin, Meks, Lootas remnants) hit the gate often in evaluation; how many of those flipped a decision was not measured per game. Bench (mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy, 1 pair, candidate seat): game M1 50 lines (16 combo exclusions), game M2 41 lines (13 combo exclusions) - mean 45.5 per game; fires only in the candidate seat (BASE has no such tag). Pair margin E -6.0 (n=1, noise, not a result).
risks: (1) Fires often in evaluation with Orks (many cheap remnants in charge range); each fire lowers a remnant's value, so the AI may leave more nearly dead units alive in melee range - those can still score OC on objectives, hold secondaries (e.g. a 1-model remnant on an objective, or keep the opponent from Assassination/No Prisoners-type kill cards for us). Mitigation: ch_can_wipe/ch_can_halve (+8) and objective/short-charge multipliers still reward the kill, and only the overkill part of ch_damage is removed. (2) Dropping a remnant from multi-target combos can lose real value when the geometry DOES allow engaging both (remnant + main target): the old EV credited ~20% extra; post-roll re-pick still covers low rolls. (3) Full-game effect untested (rounds 3-5 lesson: one-round rollouts miss later scoring); the ratio 2.0 is a judgement value, picked to leave the measured guardrails (1.02x, 1.27x) untouched. (4) The [CHARGE_TARGET] log fires on evaluations, not only on changed decisions, so fire counts overstate decision changes.
